description.narrative:
People in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), which is the outbreak's epicenter, with all 26 provinces affected. In DRC, Mpox has impacted urban and rural communities, with certain provinces experiencing particularly high transmission rates.
Bordering countries to the east of DRC—notably Burundi, Rwanda, and Uganda—where the risk of cross-border transmission is high due to proximity and recent case reports.
Additional African nations reporting outbreaks or importation of cases, including Kenya, South Africa, Nigeria, Central African Republic, and Côte d'Ivoire. These countries, some of which have endemic levels of Mpox, face expanding or re-emerging outbreaks.
High-risk groups within these populations, such as children, people in remote or underserved areas, sex workers, and communities with limited access to healthcare, are prioritized for surveillance, vaccination, and mental health support.

The appeal outlines a multi-tiered strategy for National Societies to respond to the epidemic. The approach includes community-based health promotion, disease surveillance, mental health support, clinical care, and vaccination, as well as water, sanitation, and hygiene initiatives. Additionally, there is a focus on socio-economic protection for affected individuals through cash assistance and livelihood support.

The response is designed to reach 30 million people directly through health services, vaccination programs, and community support, with an overarching goal of protecting a broader population of 300 million people across affected regions.

This emergency appeal addresses the escalating Mpox epidemic in Africa, which has shown a significant rise in cases and fatalities across 12 African countries, with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) at its epicenter. The IFRC aims to mitigate the health, social, and economic impacts of Mpox on affected communities through a coordinated response.

Through a three-stage approach, the IFRC will support National Societies depending on their specific epidemic status. Operations include setting up health surveillance, engaging with communities to prevent spread, training volunteers, and leveraging partnerships for vaccine administration and psychosocial support. Cross-border coordination and collaboration with national governments and international partners ensure comprehensive coverage. The IFRC’s extensive African network enables efficient resource mobilization and community outreach across affected regions.
